import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    dim_emp_hist = inputs["dim_emp_hist"].copy()
    asof_queries = inputs["asof_queries"].copy()
    
    # Perform the point-in-time join
    # For each query, find the history record where:
    # - emp_id matches
    # - as_of_date >= eff_start_date (start INCLUSIVE)
    # - eff_end_date IS NULL OR as_of_date < eff_end_date (end EXCLUSIVE)
    
    # Merge on emp_id first
    merged = asof_queries.merge(dim_emp_hist, on="emp_id", how="inner")
    
    # Apply the date range conditions
    # Condition 1: as_of_date >= eff_start_date
    condition1 = merged["as_of_date"] >= merged["eff_start_date"]
    
    # Condition 2: eff_end_date IS NULL OR as_of_date < eff_end_date
    condition2 = (merged["eff_end_date"].isna()) | (merged["as_of_date"] < merged["eff_end_date"])
    
    # Apply both conditions
    filtered = merged[condition1 & condition2]
    
    # Select output columns
    asof_result = filtered[["query_id", "emp_id", "dept", "grade"]].copy()
    
    # Sort to ensure consistent ordering (by query_id, emp_id, then by start date descending
    # to handle ties - most recent version first, though inner join should give us one row per query)
    asof_result = asof_result.sort_values(by=["query_id", "emp_id"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    return {"asof_result": asof_result}
